title: The Kiwi Chronicles
content:
Cutti: Mattuuuu, are you excited to visit your favorite country?

Cutti asked, phone camera already pointed at my face, because annoying me on video is her life's purpose.

I yawned so wide my jaw cracked.

Me: Yeeeesss

I replied with full joshh and a sleep-deprived expression. Hehe.

We had left Bengaluru on Feb 28th. Layover in Singapore, then Sydney, then Christchurch — more than 24 hours of flying, or maybe it just felt like that because we were chasing the east side of the globe and those guys are always ahead of us in time. Four of us. Me, my wife Pavithra (Cutti), my cousin Rithesh (Rinku), and Harini (Farini).

And the plan? Campervan. An RV. Our first ever. After Iceland, this was the one thing all four of us had been drooling over for months.

Day 1 · 01/03/2026

Christchurch → Fairlie

We landed in Christchurch around 3PM and were already running late. Britz, the company we had hired our campervan from, runs a free airport shuttle. We missed it. Obviously. What's the fun if we don't arrive late, eh? Every single time, lol.

Booked an Uber and literally ran into the Britz office.

Attendee: We are almost closing for the day, we cannot give you the van today

My heart dropped. If he said no, that's a full day gone — one day of a 14-day trip, plus a hotel we hadn't booked. We begged. Flight delays, long journey, first time in NZ, the whole sob story. He softened and agreed to hand over the keys. Only problem — everyone else had left for the day. No walkthrough. No demo. No instructions.

So we tossed a coin and took the wheel saying we'll figure it out.

Figure out WHAT exactly? We had absolutely no clue how to operate an RV. We knew how to steer and how to move it forward. That's it. How to refill fresh water, how to dump the waste, how the toilet works, where the storage boxes are, how the gas works — zero.

Bro, this is a 4-berth house on wheels, and you have never even parked an Innova properly; my inner-me reminded me as I climbed into the driver's seat.

It was raining. We didn't care. Pulled out towards Lake Tekapo with me driving and Rinku in the passenger seat reading the manual with such intensity that I'm fairly sure he'd have cleared every single engineering subject in one attempt if he had ever read like that in college, lol.

Campsites in NZ come in two flavours. Powered ones — mostly private, expensive, but you get shared kitchen, washrooms, hot showers. And unpowered ones — dirt cheap or completely free, like DOC campsites and freedom camping spots, usually parked right on a lakeside with a view that'll make you forget what a washroom even is.

The only thing they told us at the counter was this: look for plug-in campsites, the battery might need charging.

Why do I need a shared kitchen when I'm literally driving a full kitchen, I thought.

We stopped at Fairlie campsite, plugged in to charge, and by then it was almost evening. Cooked dinner, poked around the vehicle opening every cupboard like curious monkeys.

Temperature had dropped to 4°C. It was bloody cold. We just cuddled into those tiny cute beds and slept.

Day 2 · 02/03/2026

Fairlie → Lake Tekapo → Lake Pukaki

You know how the first proper morning of a trip feels, right? Full excitement, full hopes, zero idea what's coming. That was us.

Before taking the wheel again, we decided to actually learn our house. Checked the gas, figured out how to refill water, found where the battery percentage shows. And the big discovery of the morning — the campervan charges itself while we drive. So do we really need to pay for powered campsites every night just to charge? That became our little experiment for the rest of the trip.

Breakfast was Kiran Sandwichwala's signature Lemon Semiya, straight from our Bengaluru stash. We still had to shop for bread, eggs and milk, so it was a light one, and we took the wheel to Lake Tekapo — the first stop for pretty much every traveller in the South Island.

The weather was moderate today. And is this really a lake? It spans like 25–30 km.

Lake Tekapo is an alpine lake — a lake that sits up in the mountain ranges. Most lakes in NZ are fed by glacier rivers. When there's a heavy flow, the water looks greenish because of fine sand being carried along. Once the sediment settles, you get that unreal turquoise blue.

It was way more beautiful than we had imagined. We took a leisurely stroll along the lakefront, found a picturesque bench and got some candids there.

Farini: Ritheshhh, what about lupins? Where are they?

Rinku: How would I know? They were supposed to be here on the lakefront.

Blunt reply, like always. To be honest, we hadn't really planned this trip. With the campervan we didn't have to worry about stays, so we let it go fully impromptu. Lupins? Not in March, apparently.

The Church of the Good Shepherd was right there at eyesight distance. Only Rinku and Farini went near to take pictures. Me and Cutti just chilled by the lake.

Next was the Tasman Glacier viewpoint, so we drove along Lake Pukaki — another turquoise blue lake, another woah moment 😛

On the way we stopped at a lavender farm that had no lavender. They had just harvested everything, so all we saw were plants. Grabbed a lavender-flavoured ice-cream and moved on.

We were driving through the same landscapes every Instagram reel shows off, except ours were brown. March is the end of summer in NZ, kind of a dry season, so the mountains were dry.

You might ask why we still went in this season. Well, we picked NZ for the adventure activities and the campervan life. We had already done our landscape hunting in Iceland, haha.

It was around 5 PM when we parked and started the trail to the Tasman Glacier viewpoint. A short hike, about 20 mins one way, around 1.5 km. On the way you see little blue lakes formed by the glaciers, and at the top there's the lake right in front of you with the Tasman Glacier behind it. Minimum effort, maximum pleasure kind of a thing.

Nobody else was there except us. Good banter, cool pictures, and by 7 PM we started back.

NZ gets around 13–14 hours of daylight at this time of the year, so your evenings are long and you can enjoy them a lot.

We drove to the Lake Pukaki free campsite. It welcomed us with a dark sky, hundreds of campervans and millions of stars. We cooked hot hot rasam, served it with rice and yoghurt, and had dinner under a full moon. Cherry on the cake? We got a lovely video of that moment.

The campsite was genuinely free, no surprises. Except there were no washrooms. We had used the ones at the Tasman viewpoint and then the campervan's own loo, so we planned to sort ourselves out in Twizel the next day.

Public toilets in NZ are super clean. The only exceptions are the dry toilets, which you mostly find at free lakeside campsites.

Day 3 · 03/03/2026

Mt Cook → Twizel → Queenstown

Alarm at 4 AM. We were an hour away from Mt Cook, and fortunately there were no tantrums from our wives — we left almost on the mark.

Packed in layers of fleece and jackets, we started the Hooker Valley Track a little later than planned, around 6:15. The snow-capped mountains ahead were luring us in. As we walked, the sun came up and we caught a proper golden hour — orange hues spreading across the whole alpine range.

The Hooker Valley Track is about 5 km one way and fairly easy — gravel paths, boardwalks and three big swing bridges. The Hooker River runs along the whole valley with that milky light-blue colour, which comes from fine rock particles called "glacial flour". The first bridge crosses right where Mueller Lake feeds out.

The last bridge was under construction, so we couldn't go all the way to the end. We stopped at the last open one and soaked in the warm sunlight with the river and the alps in front of us. Was it worth it? Ask a mountain lover. 1000% worth it, hahah.

Back at the parking, we cooked eggs, peeled oranges and had breakfast staring at snow-capped mountains.

inner-me: Take a bath, man.

My inner me mocked me. It had been three days, lol.

We drove to Twizel, a cute little town. Used the public restrooms, and then what? We went to the Twizel community pool. Swim, float, then a hot shower after three days. Such a refreshing feeling it was.

Twizel also had a spot to refill fresh water and dump waste, so we finished our campervan rituals. Sounds fun. Doing it is not.

Fuelled up and off to the famous Queenstown. Even dry, the route was so scenic. We crossed Lindis Pass and stopped at the viewpoint. Cutti had been sleeping through the whole drive, so I took some pictures without her.

Cutti: Why didn't you wake me up?

Me: We did, but you were in such deep sleep, you said you won't come and we should go enjoy the view.

Me, Farini and Rinku had agreed to play with her for a while. Thankfully, we were all on the same page :-P She figured out later that we never actually woke her. The weather had flipped by then too — fully sunny, nothing like the last two days.

I took a good nap after Lindis Pass and Rinku drove till Queenstown. First stop? Fergburger. How did we find it? Our master finder for these things, Ms Fariniii, the one who knows every food spot and café wherever we go.

Long line for one big burger. I was still knocked out, so they all went and got me one. Bless them.

We hadn't booked a campsite. Everything in Queenstown was full, so we drove a bit further to 12 Mile Delta. Burger, beer, done.

Perk of a full Queenstown? It was blood moon day and we watched it from 12 Mile Delta. Millions of stars with a red moon hanging in the middle. Perfect picture.

The total lunar eclipse on 3 March 2026 was the only one of the year, and the last blood moon visible worldwide until late 2028.

We wrapped up the day. And tonight it was our turn to sleep on the bigger bed 😛

Day 4 · 04/03/2026

Queenstown, adventure day

Woke up to a beautiful sunrise over Wilson Bay on Lake Wakatipu, right where the 12 Mile Delta campsite is. We had the Shotover Jet at 10:30 AM, so we had to be early. Iceland's Silfra fissure delays had taught us that lesson.

I took a small stroll to the lake and stretched out. Freshened up, spread the table, cut oranges, cooked breakfast and kick-started adventure day.

First up, the Shotover Jet, named after the Shotover River where it runs. At first it felt like a normal jet boat. But hold your horses — that 360-degree spin, omg.

Me: How would it be to be a jet boat driver?

inner-me: Yeah, seems like a more stable job than IT in the age of AI.

My inner me stated a blunt fact. I told my wife I wanted to be a jet boat driver and settle down in Queenstown. She dismissed it like I wasn't serious. Which, fair, I'm mostly not 😛

Crazy spins, one of a kind, seriously awesome.

Next, the Kawarau swing. We wanted to bungee too, but there were no slots. Me and Cutti did the couple swing, Rinku went solo. Fariniii is scared of these activities and skipped it.

I was scared too, you can see it in the video, lol. I'm afraid of heights, but I still do it every time. The only way to get rid of fear is to keep doing it more and more.

Then the confusion started in my head — bungee at Kawarau or Nevis?

Rinku: Do it at Nevis.

Nevis is 143 m. Kawarau is just 43 m. I've already done 83 m in Rishikesh, so why go lower now?

While I was still battling with courage, desire, fear and the challenge, Rinku wanted to cliff jump, so we drove to Little Thailand. Man, that was a serious thing. Nobody at the spot and we weren't even sure it was the right place. Just then a local and his friend came up after jumping, so okay, this is the spot. Me and Rinku hiked down about 100 metres to the jump point.

At first I thought I'd try. I had never jumped without a life jacket, and this was the real deal — no safety, no life jacket, nobody to pull you out if you drown. Real shit.

Rinku looked at the depth. Easily 45 ft. He gasped and sat down for a minute.

inner-me: Okay boy, this one is definitely not yours.

I listened. Not without someone there to help. And while I was still processing, Rinku jumped. Omg, what a feeling it was for him. He came up so happy.

Fun fact — he actually jumped from a little higher than the proper spot. He only noticed the clean jumping ledge while climbing back up, lol.

We were all so content, with many more adventures to go. Had good fish — monk and blue cod — and then some pretty gelato at Ferg.

By evening, the girls were curious about Hydro Attack, a semi-submarine ride that dives in and out of the water. Cool for them, not so much for the boys 😛 No slots anyway, so we headed to the Luge.

Six rounds of luge on the Arrow and Dart tracks brought out the inner child in all of us. A luge is a small cart you sit in and control the speed yourself as it runs down the track. First round was decent. From the second, we raced non-stop.

Adventure in Queenstown costs a fortune. The Kawarau couple swing was 240 NZD per person (~₹12,500). Shotover Jet plus Luge came to around ₹16,000 per person.

Milford Sound was the next day, so we decided to do the remaining activities on the way back and drove to the Lumsden campsite, en route to Milford.

Day 5 · 05/03/2026

Lumsden → Te Anau → Milford Sound

We had booked the last Milford cruise at 3:30, so it was a leisurely start. Lumsden was a good campground — water refill, waste dump, everything in one place. Finished all the campervan chores and left.

We drove via Lake Te Anau. Beautiful, but as usual we were running late, so we decided to stop on the way back. We had no plans for the night anyway because we didn't know where we'd halt, lol. Told you, we're fully impromptu sometimes.

This drive was completely different. Dense forest everywhere — a proper Western Ghats feeling.

The south-west of NZ is mostly wet, full of dense forest and fiords, while the central part is all glaciers and alpine ranges.

We boarded the boat and it was the best sight. As we sailed, the captain explained Milford's history and geography. Some of the mountains there have unique compositions, and apparently might even contain gold. Not sure about that.

There was no rain, so it didn't look like the moody social media version. Still very beautiful — giant mountains standing straight out of the water, and waterfalls like Lady Bowen and Stirling Falls that were worth the trip by themselves.

Milford Sound is actually a fiord, not a sound. A fiord is carved out by glaciers, a sound by rivers. It looks like a sound today, but historically it was glaciers that did the carving.

On the drive back to Lumsden we stopped at Te Anau for sunset and some chill time. It got dark pretty soon, so we couldn't spend much time by the lake.

Long day, but worth it. Late dinner and sleep with no alarm for the next morning, lol. It was so windy that night we genuinely wondered if the campervan would fall apart. We and our crazy thoughts.

Day 6 · 06/03/2026

Lumsden → Queenstown (Nevis Bungy)

How fun it is to have a slow morning with zero plans, where all you need to think about is where to take a bath, lol.

We finished our campervan no-fun rituals and went for a swim. There was a community pool nearby — paid at the shop opposite the campsite and walked through the neighbourhood to get there.

Community pools in NZ usually have hot showers, and they're the best way to shower on a campervan trip. Around 3–5 NZD per person (~₹150–250).

Let me kill a myth here. A campervan doesn't really reduce your expenses compared to hotels, taxis or a rental car. What it gives you is complete freedom — camping on lakesides and beautiful spots, and a totally different feel. It also adds a lot of tasks to your plate: cooking, cleaning the vehicle, dumping waste. But that's the fun. Be careful though, it's extremely addictive. At least for me it was.

We sat down to figure out the day and decided to go back to Queenstown and maybe do the bungee. I still wasn't sure. Cutti was even more hesitant.

While Rinku took the wheel, I grabbed my credit card and booked the Nevis slot. No seeing and all after reaching. I will definitely not back out once I've paid, lol. Paisa vasool guy, I am 😛

Cutti said she'd do Kawarau. So the plan was — I report at the AJ Hackett office for the Nevis shuttle, and Rinku and Farini drive Cutti to Kawarau.

I took the shuttle, fully nervous. 143 m, 441 ft, is no joke for an acrophobic like me. Played some music, gathered courage and reached the place. A long iron cable stretched between two mountains, and in the middle hangs a big box, which is where you jump from. Forget the view from the box — I was shit scared just looking at the setup from the edge of the mountain.

Somehow I got into the cable car that carries you out to the box. I was third in line. One thing I was sure of: however scared I am, I'm doing it, because I've paid for it, lol.

All geared up, I stood on the edge. I still don't remember how I fell. I opened my eyes somewhere in between and it was so smooth and satisfying. You fall, bounce back up a bit, and fall again — way smoother than Rishikesh. After the second bounce there's a rope you pull, which clips the cord near your stomach so you flip into a sitting position and just enjoy the view.

Me: Fyck yeashhhh, I finally did it!

Capturing your fear is a crazy feeling. I got on the bus so happy and called them to tell them I did it and to ask about Cutti's jump.

Guess what? They had taken their sweet time shopping souvenirs at DF Souvenirs, and by the time they asked, the last slot was gone. I only found out when I called them on the way back.

I got so pissed. But it was going to be her first jump, so we said we'll see tomorrow, and chilled at Boundary Street park. Thankfully, we found free parking right there. Queenstown evenings are something else — pinkish golden hour, families playing sports in the park. It made us question the busy lives we live back in our cities.

Celebrations for the jump? Good beer and another Fergburger. Day wrapped.

And we slept excited for the next day — skydive day. First skydive for all of us, except Rinku.

Day 7 · 07/03/2026

Wanaka Skydive → Queenstown → Bendigo

Skydive day, yaaay. We had the 10:30 morning slot, so we freshened up, cooked breakfast and left for Wanaka.

At Skydive Wanaka they briefed us, suited us up, and then, guess what.

Guide: Hey, we have to push your booking. There are clouds and no visibility.

No promise of when they'd fly again. We could take a refund, wait as long as we liked, or reschedule. We moved it to 2:30 and drove to the community centre to shower and freshen up. Came back an hour early just to be double sure, and yes, we were suited up again.

So tense, and so thrilled.

Farini: I am not going first.

She told her diver to take her last. As usual, Rinku went first, me second, Cutti third and Fariniii last.

My first skydive. I was so lost in the view that I didn't notice my diver tapping my shoulder — that's the signal to spread your arms for the photos. He kept tapping, and I only realised at the very end, lol.

Still got some pictures, and the view of Lake Wanaka and Lake Hāwea from up there was unreal. The landing was sooo smooth. Best experience ever. Absolutely loved it.

What next? We had to start heading north, so we decided to drive via Queenstown and get Cutti her bungee today. We had just a 40-minute gap before the Hydro Attack slot we had booked for the evening.

Cutti: Mattu, we'll do it in Rishikesh, it's fine.

Me: We'll do Rishikesh also. We're doing it here.

I called AJ Hackett — no slots. I decided to drive by and check at the counter anyway. Ran to the booking desk, begged for a slot, and we got one. While she went to change, I asked them to send her soon after their lunch break as we had another activity. They agreed, and Cutti was third in line.

I stood on the viewing deck thinking this money is gone. Honestly, I wasn't sure she'd make it.

She stood on the board, and there she goes — a perfect bungee leap. I screamed yaaaay. So happy and so proud of my brave girl. She definitely beat my expectations, huh? Lol.

Collected her complimentary T-shirt and went for Hydro Attack, which then got cancelled because of high tides. Twice unlucky with that one.

Now we headed north, onto the glacier route. Franz Josef was a 5-hour drive and we didn't want to rush, so we camped at Bendigo, on the Clutha River, just an hour away.

We reached around 7 PM, perfect sunset time. Put out the table and chairs and had one of the best quality evenings of the trip. Me and Cutti walked down to the Clutha River and cherished the whole evening.

Cutti: Mattu, let's swim with dolphins.

She was thinking of the crazy dolphin swim at Kaikōura. Me and Rinku looked at each other in despair. Just when we'd finished all the unplanned stuff, here was another one, and of course we were all equally excited.

The problem was, we weren't sure about going up to Wharariki. It's a long drive.

Me: Macha, let's do it. We'll just drive a bit more each day and do the full circuit.

Why would the group say no? And despite this whole idea, we never bothered to book the dolphins, lol. We and our last-minute bookings.

Day 8 · 08/03/2026

Bendigo → Wanaka → Haast → Lake Paringa

The washrooms at Bendigo were dry toilets, so we started early and drove to Lake Wanaka to freshen up.

What a peaceful life, I thought, watching people take their boats out on the lake. Parents letting their kids play by the water. Kids kayaking. Locals on morning walks. Life skills and health over everything else. How cool is it to wake up, walk to a lake and have fun? I miss that in the cities we live in. NZ is such a balanced country for quality of life — if you want a big social life, though, it's not the place.

Me: I wanna be in Wanaka.

Farini: Yeah, you wanna be a Shotover Jet driver, you wanna be in Queenstown, now Wanaka. What all you want to be? Have some clarity.

Heh.

And you might be wondering why we kept going back and forth between Queenstown and Wanaka. That's what impromptu planning gives you — no fixed itinerary, stay flexible, come back with no regrets. Sure, we could have booked everything in advance. But it ran this way and it was okay. I love that Rinku and Farini sail with the same mindset and are at peace with it. Cheers.

After an hour or so we left. First stop was the Lake Hāwea viewpoint, the same lake I had admired from the skydive. Too sunny, so we glanced at it and moved on.

The road to Franz Josef is packed with falls, creeks and offbeat spots. First up, Blue Pools.

inner-me: Fresh glacier water. Why not take a dip?

Me and Rinku went ahead while the wives walked like tortoises. The water was freezing and biting. I slowly got in and couldn't stay for more than a minute, it was that freaking cold. Took a short break and went in again. Never been in water that cold. Felt great and energised after.

But the sandflies, man. They're a huge issue in NZ. They irritated us so much we had to leave.

Next was a creek. Farini and Rinku stayed back, Me and Cutti went in. To see it properly you have to walk through water above ankle depth, and it was shit cold again. The numbness and biting nearly made Cutti give up until I told her to take a breath and try again. Thanks to my Blue Pools dip, I was kind of used to it.

Google says a creek is a narrow piece of water entering the land from the sea. The creeks here were different. This one had a huge rock split open like a cave with water flowing through it.

inner-me: Go climb that rock and take a picture.

My inner me finally said something useful, and I got one, lol.

Fantail Falls and Thunder Creek came next, but we were exhausted, so we saw them from a distance and got back on the wheel.

By then we had to dump the waste water and refill fresh water, which we did at Haast. I was done driving for the day and slept at the back while Rinku drove to the Lake Paringa campsite near Franz Josef. We wrapped up with dreams of flying over a glacier the next day. My first helicopter ride, haha.

Day 9 · 09/03/2026

Lake Matheson → Glacier Heli → Hokitika Gorge → Punakaiki

Rinku got up early and drove us to Lake Matheson for a sunrise walk around the circuit.

Me: Wow, whatta perfect reflection.

I said it to myself. The circuit goes past two lakes, and both of them mirror the mountains and forest around them perfectly.

Lake Matheson has eels, which are traditionally harvested by Māori for cultural festivals. Otherwise they're hard to catch, and people aren't allowed in the lake.

Rinku: Okay, hurry up, we're getting late for the glacier ride.

We had to be there by 10:30. We were all so excited. Finished the checks and formalities and boarded the chopper.

The ride went over Fox Glacier, and the captain explained the name — the end of the glacier looks like a fox's tail. We landed on the glacier and, as usual, it was fun time. Grabbed fresh snow and threw it at each other. Me and Rinku tasted some ice too, lol. Got some really cool pictures and flew back to Franz Josef.

We were tired. Quick lunch, then straight to Hokitika Gorge.

inner-me: Creek, gorge... what are all these out-of-dictionary words?

A gorge is a valley between two steep mountain slopes with water flowing through the middle.

Hokitika felt like Blue Pools, just greener and calmer. We didn't bother getting in. We just sat there and forgot all our worries for a while, until the sandflies chased us out :-P

Another long drive today. We were heading to Wharariki Beach the next day, and our trick was simple: no plan, just drive a bit more every day. What else do you have a motorhome for?

Sunset at the Punakaiki Pancake Rocks. They're named after the pancake-like layers in the rock.

The Pancake Rocks are limestone, built from the shells and skeletons of ancient marine life that settled on the seabed. Tectonic uplift then pushed them up above sea level, where wind and waves carved those pancake layers.

Wharariki was another 6 hours away, so we decided to halt at the Wai-iti Domain campsite — 4 hours from Punakaiki, about 2 from Wharariki.

Rinku: Macha, you drive now, I'll drive in the morning.

Because he knows I won't get up on time in the morning. Played some songs, often listening to Cutti's snoring, lol. She was supposed to give me company but chose to snore.

We finally arrived, and it was nothing like the other sites. Just a plain empty ground. Felt like a haunted place, but I was too tired to give a damn. Pulled down my bed and crashed.

Day 10 · 10/03/2026

Wharariki Beach → Motueka → Kaikōura

I dreamt that someone was shaking me really hard to wake me up. It wasn't a dream. Rinku was shaking me. He had got up early and already driven us to Wharariki, lol.

It was around 8 AM. We freshened up in the parking lot, made breakfast and decked up. There's a "short" hike from the parking to the beach, that's what they said :-P It's just 1 km, but it did not feel short.

After the hike, there's another few hundred metres of sand to the shore. The constant heavy winds have formed dunes, and walking on them is tiring — your feet sink in and it takes extra effort to pull them out for every step.

inner-me: Ah, pristine white sand beach. Like any other country.

My inner me amused me as we reached the shore. Wharariki is famous for being a Windows lock screen. It was beautiful, but too sunny to really enjoy. Crazy, dramatic rock formations — more dramatic than Farini when she's convincing us to go to some cool café 😛

We tried to recreate the Windows lock screen. Thanks to our zero-skill photography, we never figured out the angle that photographer used. Still got some good shots and chilled for a while.

Me: Come on, let's go for a spa day.

You know us. Every trip of ours ends with a bath, a spa, something like that. I said the spa was very close by. Everyone asked why none of them had seen it on Google, but they trusted me fully. Only when I started navigating did I realise I had been looking at a spa in Rotorua. On the North Island. Dammit.

Anyway, by now Kaikōura was definitely on, so it was time to book the dolphin swim. We and our never-ending last-minute plans.

Luck wasn't on our side. Every slot at Dolphin Encounter, the famous company, was sold out. There was another operator with not-so-great reviews, but still okay. Dolphin Encounter put us on a waiting list in case someone cancelled, and we started driving east anyway. If it didn't work out, we'd go with the other agency.

On the way we stopped at Motueka for a hot shower.

We were back on the road when Rinku's phone rang from an unknown number.

Rinku: Stop the music.

He talked very seriously while we all wondered what had happened.

Rinku: Yes, yes, we'll take the slot for the dolphin swim at 8:30!

He was jumping, haha.

It was dusk by then and we started the heavy ghat section. Past 11 PM, I was driving, and Rinku had fallen asleep in the bed above the driver's seat. I was doing around 70 km/h when I noticed a police car behind me with its lights on. I thought they were just patrolling. A minute later the siren started. I pulled the campervan to the side of the road, and a cute cop walked up. I'm not bluffing, she was really cute, man.

Cop: Sir, can I see your licence?

After checking the documents, she said I was speeding — the limit within town is 50 km/h. I said sorry. She entered my details on her phone, took a photo, told me to follow the speed signs, and was kind enough to let us go without a fine. Not just cute, but polite and respectful.

Oh, and she told me I'd be fined next time if a passenger was sleeping in the back while the campervan was moving. We had no idea. Damn, this is exactly what we'd have learnt if we had reached Britz on time on Day 1.

Rinku and Farini sat with their seat belts on for a while, then went back to bed once we were out of town limits. Finally reached the Kaikōura campsite at 1 AM, and I crashed like always, with sweet dreams of swimming with dolphins.

Day 11 · 11/03/2026

Kaikōura Dolphin Swim → Christchurch

Guess what? Rinku woke up at 8. He had missed his alarm. Thank god the dolphin swim centre was just 10 minutes away. Everyone woke up, did a 2-minute freshen-up and rushed to the reporting spot.

While me and Rinku checked in and did the formalities, Farini and Cutti made bread and hummus, which we ate during the training. After a quick briefing on handling the wetsuit, how to swim, and the etiquette of interacting with dolphins, we headed out into the Pacific.

Masked up and geared, we waited for the captain's first honk, and swoosh — we all jumped in.

Omg, seriously, whattta feeling. Hundreds of dolphins passing right under you. Sometimes you end up touching them without even trying. I genuinely run out of words to describe it. We saw dolphins breaching — jumping right out of the water — and spinners that leap into the air and spin several times before landing.

At the second honk, everyone climbs back on the boat and they go looking for another pod so you can jump in again. You get to do it 5 times. Totally paisaaa vasool. One of a kind.

We were shit tired after that and hadn't had a proper breakfast, so we drove to the South Bay campsite for breakfast-cum-lunch. This was almost the end of our South Island trip. We stopped at Pak'nSave to stock up on Tim Tams and chocolates, then drove to a beach campsite in Christchurch and halted for the night.

Day 12 · 12/03/2026

Christchurch → Auckland

One last day in Christchurch. We had planned a lot to explore and missed all of it. Why? Damn campervan rituals.

Before returning the van, we had to clean it and clear out all the waste. If we had taken the special package for around 250 NZD (~₹13,000) extra, we could have returned it as it was — no cleaning, no refilling gas or petrol, nothing. Who knew we'd end up spending almost 230 NZD (~₹12,000) just on gas and fuel refills anyway.

Cleaning took about an hour and a half, then refilling the cooking gas and petrol. One last stop at a DF Souvenirs nearby to take home a kiwi.

We handed over the campervan and flew to Auckland.

For the North Island it was just two days, so we switched to a car — a Toyota RAV4 — and drove towards Waitomo for the next day's cave tour, halting at an Airbnb.

Honestly, I wouldn't suggest doing it our way. We wasted a full day on campervan duties and the flight. We weren't sure about Kaikōura or going north, so we thought driving the campervan up would be a waste of effort and fuel. Now I feel driving is better than waiting around like a dumb at the airport for a short transfer.

Day 13 · 13/03/2026

Waitomo → Rotorua

We were almost at the end of the trip, adventures mostly done, and yet there was another exciting moment — meeting Cutti's friend Nannaiah. Now he's all our friend, haha.

We woke up a bit early at our cozy Airbnb and cooked some food. The day belonged to Nannaiah's plan: Waitomo Caves first, then whatever he suggested, since he lives in Hamilton.

At Waitomo we took the boat ride, and wow. Glow worms all over the ceiling of the limestone caves, a sight to behold. Limestone caves are naturally a bit shiny, but the glow worms add a pure greenish glow to the darkness, and that's another beauty altogether.

We had to keep our phones on silent so as not to disturb the place, and our pictures came out blurry. Just when I was wondering why our Fariniii wasn't hungry yet...

Farini: Let's go somewhere to eat no, I'm already hungryy.

Haha, timing matched.

We drove to Rotorua and had lunch at Lime Café on the lakeside.

Nannaiah: Rotorua is where the first zorb was invented. You'd love to try?

One more adventure? Why not. It was already late and the last zorb slot was at 4, so I ran to the counter and got 5 tickets. There are different tracks to choose from, and we picked the swirly zig-zag one to keep it fun.

Just when we were wondering what next...

Me: Why don't we go to that spa I thought was near Wharariki? It's in Rotorua anyway, right?

Everyone: Hmmm, not a bad idea, let's go.

Nannaiah had other plans and headed back to Hamilton, promising to meet us the next day. We went to Hell's Gate.

Hell's Gate is NZ's geothermal mud spa. Again we were racing closing time, and guess what? We walked in, paid, and they shut the counters right behind us, lol. We need to work on our timings for sure, eh? Hehe.

The Hell's Gate mud spa runs in three parts: a 20-minute soak in warm, mineral-rich volcanic mud, then a cool plunge or waterfall rinse, and finally the naturally heated sulphur pools.

It was unforgettable for two reasons. One, it was our first mud spa. Two, damn, everyone's skin started itching, except Rinku, who fell sick instead. Something in that mud or sulphur didn't suit us. Not trying that again.

After a whole day of running, we got back to our Airbnb by the Redwoods, cooked biryani and rasam rice, and slept.

Day 14 · 14/03/2026

Blue Spring → McLaren Falls → Auckland

We all woke up already missing New Zealand. My dreams of living in Wanaka, Cutti and Farini wanting to live in Queenstown — all going back to being just dreams.

We had kept it a leisure day. Cooked one last semiya, sipped one last coffee at the BnB, and agreed to meet Nannaiah at the Blue Spring.

The Blue Spring near Putāruru is a massive freshwater spring — they say a big share of NZ's bottled water comes from here. The trail walks you along it, with boards on its history and how Māori protected the water and their villages.

That was officially the end of sightseeing. We stopped at McLaren Falls, grabbed pizzas from Pizza Jack and crashed in the nearby park. Played Uno, had long banters, made fun of each other and took a quick power nap. What a day to end a trip.

And we weren't the only ones. So many New Zealanders camp in these public parks — barbecue, beers and family time. Truly balanced.

We drove through the city, grabbed gelato, took an evening walk on the beach, and then it was time to say bye to NZ and to Nannaiah.

We drove to Auckland airport under orange sunset skies, said bye to Nannaiah, dropped off the car and boarded the flight with heavy hearts and full memories.

This one was harder to leave than any other trip. It was our last trip of the year with Rinku and Farini before they move to the US in a month or two.

So, until next time — Mā te wā. 🥝

So Day 6 wrapped with beer, Fergburger, and golden hour at Boundary Street. Day 7 — what happened next? Did Cutti finally get her Kawarau jump in?
Oh yeah, we also slept looking forward to the next day as it was sky diving, all of our first sky dive except Rinku's

Oh, sky diving! That's huge — and Rinku's already a pro while the rest of you are first-timers. Tell me everything about Day 7 — how'd the skydive go, did Cutti get her Kawarau jump too, and what was going through your heads before jumping out of a plane?

It was a skydive day, yaaay. We were excited so much; we had a morning slot at 10:30, so we freshened up and cooked breakfast and left to Wanaka

We went to SkyDive Wanaka NZ which is the company we had booked skydive, we were prepped with instructions and suited up, guess what
“Hey, we have to push your booking as there clouds and no visibility”, the guide said

They did not give us any hopes of when they might do it again, we could opt for refund or wait as long as we want or reschedule too. We rescheduled it to 2:30 and drove to Community Centre where there was a shower and we could freshen up

We freshened up and arrived an hour before just to be double sure and yeah, we were suited up again after the wait.

So tensed and also thrilled, and “I am not going first”, Fariniii said and he told diver to jump with her at the last

As usual, Rinku went first, me second, third cutti and last Fariniiii.

My first sky dive, I was so lost in the view, the diver is tappin on my shoulder, if he taps, we can spread our arms and enjoy the view for photograph. I was so lost, he kept tapping and I did not realise until the end, lol

Somehow got some pics and we got a good view of wanaka and hawai
 Lake, and landing? It was sooo smoooth . Best experience ever, Absolutely loved it.

What’s next? As we had to drive further up the north now, we decided we will drive via Queenstown and let Cutti do her bungy today. We had only 40 mins gap, and evening slot was booked for hydro attack. 

“Mattu, we will do in Rishikesh, it is fine”, she tried to push it today as well. I said, rishikesh also we will do no, we will do here

I called up AJ Hackett, they said no slots, I decided to drive by and check out there at counter in the site. Ran to the booking and asked her for a slot, thankfully, we got one. While she went to change, I requested to send her quick soon after their lunch break as we had another activity, the bookie agreed and cutti was third on the row to jump.

I was on the viewing deck thinking this money is gone, because, I was honestly not sure she was gonna make it.

She stood on the board, there she goes, a perfect bungee leap. I screamed yaaaay and I was so happy and proud of my brave girl. She definitely is beyond my expectations huh? Lol

I was so happy, collected her complimentary t-shirt and went to hydroattack, but was cancelled due to high tides. 

We headed towards North East of South Island, which is glacier route. Our next stop was Franz Joseph. It was an 5 hour ride, we did not wanted to rush, so we decided to camp in Bendigo Campsite which is on the Clutha River which was just an hour from there. 

We reached there by 7pm around, a perfect sunset time, put out the table and chairs and had one of the best quality time out there. Me and cutti took a small stroll towards Clutha river and cherished the whole evening. 

“Mattu, swim with dolphins”, Cutti said as we had one crazy dolphin swim at Kaikora
Me and Rinku looked in despair; just when we finished all the unplanned ones we are all equally excited to do this too. 

But we were not sure as we were kinda confused to go to whrariki or skip it as it’s gonna be a long ride. 

“Macha, let’s do. We will just drive a bit more each day and do the circuit”, I suggested and of course why would the group say no. Despite this idea, we never bothered to book that, lol
As usual we and our last minute bookings.

What a rollercoaster of a day — cloud delays, first skydives, Cutti FINALLY conquering her bungee fear ("this money is gone" 😂), and then capping it off with a gorgeous sunset at Bendigo campsite. "She definitely is beyond my expectations" is such a sweet line.

Also love that you added a whole new plan (dolphin swim at Kaikoura) without actually booking anything — very on-brand for this trip, haha.

Day 8 — tell me what happened as you continued toward Franz Joseph and the glacier route!

Since washrooms there were dry toilets, we did not wanted to freshen up there, so started our day a bit early and we drove to Wanaka lake, parked our campervan, got
What a peaceful life, I thought, looking at the some people, they had gotten their boats and was sailing on the lake

Few parents with kids had let the kids play out there, how cool it is to get up visit a lake and having fun, I miss them in cities like where we live. I mean NZ is such a cool balanced country in terms of quality of life, of course, if you’re someone who wants social life, that is not the one.

And some Kids doing the kayak and morning walks by localities emphasised life skills and health over anything 

“I wanna be in Wanaka”, I said with josh
“Yeah, you wanna be a boat driver in shotover jet, you wanna be in queenstown, now in wanaka, what all you want to be? Have some clarity”, Farinii mocked at me
Heh

And you might be wondering, how many times we go to queenstown, wanaka over and over? Well, that’s what impromptu planning gives you, no fixed itinerary, keep flexible, come back with no regrets. 
Of course, we could have booked activities well in advance and planned it up, well, it is okay, it was run rather this way. I love our partners Rinku and Farini as we all sail with same mindset and peace with it, Cheers

We left after an hour or so, on the way first stop Lake hawai
 Viewpoint, the very same like that I had admired in skydive, well, it was too sunny, just glanced a view and started again.

We had plenty of places today, enroute to franz joseph, there are some tons of falls, off beat places, creeks.

First stop was Blue pools dip, why not take a dip here? My inner me said and also fresh clear glacier water
Me n Rinku went a little head than the wives who walked lika tortoise, water was freezing cold and biting. I slowly got into the water, but could not stay longer than a min, it was that freaking cold.

I took a short break and then went in again, never got into one that was this cold, so felt great and energised, we took some pictures there, but flies are huge issues in NZ, it started to irk us a alot, so we left the place

Then came Wilson creek, Farinii n RInku did not come, Me n Cutti went in, but again water was shit cold, Cutti, almost gave up until I told her to take a breath and come again. To see the creek, we had to go into the water which was above the ankle depth, since it was extremly cold, the numbness and biting was refraining her not to come. Thanks for the blue pools dip I had, I was kinda used to it

well what’s creek? A creek is narrow piece of water entering into land from sea 

That was google def but the creeks here were diff, the Wilson creek had a huge rock cut open like a cave and a water was following through it. 
“Go climb that rock and take a picture” my inner me finally said and I got one, lol 

Next was fantail falls and Thunder Creek, was exhausted we just saw that from distant and back on the wheel. 

By then we had to unload the waste water and refill with a fresh one, we got one at Haast en route franz Joseph. 

I was done driving for the day and slept at the back while Rinku drove to Paringa Campsite closer to franz Joseph and wrapped our day with the dreams of flying over the glacier the next day and first helicopter ride of mine, haha

"You wanna be a boat driver, now in Wanaka, what all you want to be? Have some clarity" — Farini really keeping you grounded, haha! And that progression from freezing at Blue Pools to being "kinda used to it" by Wilson Creek is such a relatable cold-water battle.

Day 9 — first helicopter ride over the glacier at Franz Joseph! How'd that go? Were you nervous, and what was the view like?

Got up early and Rinku drove to lake matheson and did circuit for sunrise, 

“Wow, whatta perfect reflection”, i said to myself the lake Matheson is a circuit, with two lakes and both the lakes has perfect mirror reflection of the nature around it. It has got some eels which are mostly hunted by Māori tribe and they serves this eel as meal for their cultural festivals. Otherwise it’s difficult to even hunt for others. People can’t get into the lake as well 
Okay, hurry up, we are getting late for the glacier ride, Rinku said and we had to reach there by 10:30
We were all so excited, we finished up ore checks and formalities and boarded the chopper. 
The ride went over  the fox glacier and captain explained why it was called as fox, it’s because of the the glacier end that looks like the fox tail,
We had a landing over the glacier, as usual fun time for us, we grabbed some fresh snow and threw over each other. I and Rinku tasted some ice too, lol  
We got some really cool pictures and got back to franz Joseph. We were all tired, put some break for the quick lunch and straight to hokitika George. 

Creek, Gorge what’s all this our of dictionary words, my inner me was struggling to understand 
A Gorge is a valley between two steepy sloppy mountains with a water flowing in between. 
Hokitika was similar to blue pools but it was just green and more calmer I felt. Didn’t bother much to get into the water, we just sat there and forgot all worries for a while and enjoyed the view until sandflies troubled us to leave :-P 
We had another long journey today, the next day was wharaRiki beach, we tried to cover a lot this time despite having no plan, all we had to do was drive a bit more everyday. We had no issues and also, what else we have a motor home for? 
We had a beautiful sunset at punaikaki pancakes. A huge boulder inPunaikaki is named like that because of the pancake shape formed by the rocks, those aren’t just rocks, those are basically the limestone Rock formations because of the calcium from the dead bones of fish and marine life. It was so deep into the sea but now it’s 30-40 ft above sea level, imagine what global warming has made nowadays. 

To wharariki it was another 6 hour drive, so we decide to halt atwai iti domain campsite which is like 2 hours from wharariki and 4 hours from punaikaki.
“Macha you drive now and I will drive in the morning”, Rinku said as he knows I won’t get up on time in the morning. 
Played some songs, often listening to Cutti’s snoring, lol 
She was supposed to give me company but chose to snore
Finally we arrived at campsite but it was not like other sites, just a plain empty ground, felt like a haunted place but was too tired to even give a duck. Put my bed under and just crashed.

Throwing snow at each other on a glacier landing — what a core memory! And "played some songs, often listening to Cutti's snoring" while driving through the night to a spooky empty campsite is such a vivid closer for the day.

Day 10 — tell me about reaching Wharariki Beach! Did you end up booking that dolphin swim, or any other adventures along the way?

I had a dream that someone is shaking me so hard to wake me up, but apparently it was not the dream, Rinku shaking me to wake me up. He got up early and drove to Wharariki, lol

It was around 8am by then, we freshened up in parking, made some breakfast and decked up, It has a short hike from parking to the beach, that’s what they said :-P, but it did not feel short despite it being just 1km 

After the hike, we had to go another few hundred meters on the sand to reach the beach shore, the sand had formed dunes due to regular heavy winds and it was very tiresome to walk on that due to feet going inside and us putting additional effort to get it back and place next step

“Ah, pristine white sand beach, like any other country”, my inner me amused me as we reached the shore.

Whaririki is famous for windows lock screen image, beach was beautiful, yet too sunny to even enjoy its beauty.
It had crazy dramatic rock formations, more dramatic than Farinii when she convinces us for going to some cool cafe 😛
We tried to replicate Windows' lock screen, but thanks to our no-skill photography, where we could not figure out how that photographer really took it from what angle. We got some good shots though, chilled for a while and I said, “Come on, let us go for a spa day”

You know right? Every trip of ours usually ends with a cool bath, spa, etc. 
As we walked back, the spa was very close by, apparently I was being questioned that why Rinku, Farini, Cutti nobody saw it when they checked google. Yet they trusted me with full confidence only when I started to navigate from there, I realised I was seeing the spa that was in Rotorua, Dammit
Anyways since now we were sure of going to Kaikora, we decided we shall book Swim with dolphins. We and our last minute never ending plans, 

But luck on this day wasn’t on our side, all slots were sold out at Kaikora Dolphin, it’s a famous company. There was another one but didn’t had that great reviews. But still good 

Finally they put us on waiting list in case someone cancels their slot, we can have one, we all hoped for that and started driving in case, if we did not get this, we can go with other agency

We started driving towards the east coast to reach kaikora. En route stopped at motukeka and took hot shower. 

While we were on the run, “Stop the music”, Rinku said as he got a call from unknown number; he spoke seriously while we were all thinking what happened. 

““Yes yes, we for slot for dolphin swim on 8:30”, he was jumping, haha 


It was dusk by then, and we started driving toward the heavy ghat section; it was past 11 pm, and I was driving while Rinku had fallen asleep in the bed above the driver's seat. I was in around 70kmph and started seeing the police trailing me with the lights on, since I thought they are just patrolling, after a min, started to hear the siren too, I parked the campervan on the side of the road and a cute cop walked in, I am not bluffing, she was really cute man.

“Sir, can I see your license?”, she asked, after seeing all documents, she said I am speeding, the limit is 50kmps in town limits.
I said sorry and she entered details in her phone, took photo and said to follow the speed limit sign boards and was good enough to let us go without a fine

She wasn’t just cute, but also polite and respectable and good enough to let us go


Oh btw, she told I would be fined next time if I drive with passenger sleeping in campervan while vehicle is on the move. I did not know this, damn we should have reached early and gotten all this instructions when we got campervan.

Anyways, Rinku and Farini sat down with seat belt on for sometime and then back to bed after we left town limits. Finally it was 1am when we reached Kaikora campsite, I crashed in like always with a sweet dream of dolphins swim

Oh my god, accidentally navigating to a spa in Rotorua instead of nearby, AND getting pulled over by a cute, polite cop who let you off — what a day of plot twists! Getting that waitlist call for dolphins while driving was such perfect timing too.

Day 11 — the dolphin swim at Kaikoura! How'd it go? Were you nervous getting in the water, and what was the experience actually like?

Guess what? Rinku got up at 8 and he has missed his alarm, thank god we were close by to the Dolphin swim agency centre where we had to report, it was like 10 mins. We all woke up and quick 2 mins freshen up  & rushed towards the reporting location.

While me and Rinku went in to check in and do formalities, Farini and Cutti prepared the bread and hummus. We had it while taking the training.

After a quick brief up on wet suit handling, swim, etiquettes of interacting with dolhon, we headed into sea towards south of pacific.

We all got masked up and geared, ready for the first honk by captain, and swoosh, we all jumped into the water with our masks on.

Omg, seriously, whattta feeling, 100s of dolphins just passes by under you, sometimes you end up touching them without even wanting to. I really run out of words to express the feeling. We also saw some cool dolphins breaching meaning jumping out of water. And, also spinner, which leap into the air and spin around multiple times before landing.

Once the second honk, we need to enter back to boat and then they will wait for another pod where we can jump in again and swim with them. We can do it for 5 times, totally Paisaaa Vasoool. Really one of the kind. 


We were shit tired by then, we had not had proper breakfast, drove to south bay campsite for breakfast and lunch. Almost end of our South NZ trip, we drove to pak n save, shopped tim tams and chocolates and headed to campsite near the beach in Christchuch and halted

Swimming with 100s of dolphins and getting "Paisa Vasool" out of it five times over — incredible way to almost wrap up South Island! And the Tim Tam shopping run feels like the perfect "we're nearly done" beat.

So this is near the end of the South Island leg — are you handing back the campervan in Christchurch next, or is there more to Day 11/12? And since you started this trip wanting to explore North NZ with the RV too — walk me through what's left: the Christchurch return and the move north?

One last day at Christchurch, planned lot of things to explore but missed everything, why? Damnnn campervan rituals, we had to clean the van and clear out all waste before returning, if we had taken a special package with extra 250 nzd or something, we could have returned as it is without cleaning, refuel of gas or petrol or anything, who knew we would end up spending almost 230 nzd on gas, fuel refilling alone

It took us almost an hour and half to clean, and then fill up cooking gas and petrol, made one last stop at nearby DS Souviniers to take a kiwi for our home.


We handed ove the campervan and flew to Auckland.

We switched to car this time, as it was just two day in North NZ, rav4 Toyota and drove towards waitomo caves for the next day boating tour.

I would not suggest this as we wasted one full day for campervan duties and flight. Rather take a campervan at Auckland, drive down towards south and use ferry to cross the north - south. We had anyway planned to whrariki and kaikora which is on extreme north of south NZ, if you’re planning same, start from north and come to south and handover campervan in Christchuch, you can do it. 

We were not sure of Kaikora or entering north region right, so we thought driving one day in campervan is waste considering effort, fuel costs, etc. But now I feel driving is better than having to wait like a dumb in airport for a short transfers.

Good tip for future travelers — that logistics lesson about campervan vs flight transfer is gold for the Tips section!

So you've landed in Auckland, picked up the RAV4, and are heading to Waitomo Caves. Is this your final day (Day 12) before wrapping up the trip, or do you have more days left? Tell me about the Waitomo boating tour — what happened there, and how does the trip end?

We were almost end of our NZ trip, finished all adventures, yet another exciting moment of meeting then Cutti’s friend - Nannaiah, now he is all our friend, haha

We woke up a bit early from our cozy airbnb, cooked some food and it was all about nanniah’s plan day, we thought will do waitomo caves and then do whatever he suggests as he stays in Hamilton. 

We drove waitomo, took a boat ride and wow, glow worms in the ceiling of limestone caves was a sight to behold. Limestone caves is shinier usually in nature, but glow worms adding its pure greenish glow to the dark caves is another beauty altogether.

We were instructed to keep our phones on silent to not disturb the space, we got blurry pictures and just when I was thinking why our Fariniii is not feeling hungry, she said “Let’s go for some place to eat no, I am already hungryy”, haha, timings match

We drove to rotorua, and visited Lime Cafe on the lakeside, a good stop for lunch. 
“Rotorua is the place where the first zorb was invented; you would love to try?”, Nanniah suggested

One more adventure? Why not
It was already late and the last zorb slot was at 4, so we hurried up, I made it to booking counter and got 5 tickets to Zorb

The Zorb has various trials; we can choose what we like. We chose the swirly zig-zag track to keep it more fun, and just when we were thinking to do what’s next? 

“Why not we go to the spa that I thought it is in wharariki? Anyway, it is in Rotorua right? “, I chimed in
“Hmmm, not a bad idea, let us go”, all jinxed 

Nanniah had other plans for the day, he would meet us next day, so he went to Hamilton and we went to Hells Gate

Hells Gate is NZ geothermal mud spa, again, we had to run, since we were running out of closing time, and guess what? We entered, paid, and they shut the counters, lol
We need to work on our timings for sure eh? Hehe

Mud spa has 3 sections, where your journey begins with a rejuvenating 20-minute soak in warm, mineral-rich volcanic mud that naturally exfoliates and detoxifies your skin. Next, you will rinse off and invigorate your circulation in a refreshing cool plunge or waterfall dip before transitioning into the soothing warmth of the naturally heated sulphur mineral pools to completely melt away muscle tension. 

The experience was unforgettable for 2 reasons, one, it was our first mud spa, second, damn, everyone skin started itching except Rinku’s where he fell sick instead

There was something off in that mud or suphur but idk, not gonna try again, damn.
After continuous run, got back to Airbnb by the redwood cottage Cooked biryani and rasam rice and slept.

Meeting Nanniah and him becoming "all our friend" is such a sweet addition, and that itchy mud spa mishap (with Rinku getting sick instead!) is a perfect "logistics gone wrong" beat for the blog.

Is this the final day of the trip, or is there one more day before you fly back? And if this is the last one — any final moment before departure you want to include?

We all woke up with a feeling of missing out being in NZ, all the thoughts of me being in Wanaka, Cutti n Farini wanting to be in Queenstown is all gonna just be another dream.

We had kept it as a leisure day, cooked one last semiya, sipped one last coffee in the BnB. We coordinated with Nanniah that we will meet at Blue pools Spring. 
Blue pools spring is A massive freshwater spring located near Putāruru, they say most of the NZ supplied from here, it was a trial walk across the spring. At the end it also has its history and how Maori tribes tried to protect the water, village, etc.

We were officially done sightseeing, so we took a short stop to Mc Laren lake grabbed some pizzas at Pizza Jack, crashed at the nearby park. Played uno cards, had long banters, joked about each other, took a quick power nap. Whatta day to end the trip

Also, we were not just the people who did this, so many new zealanders do camp in these public parks, do barbeque, grab beers and have fun. Truly balanced and quality time with family 

We drove across the city, grabbed Gelato, took a eve beach walk, and it was time to bid bye to NZ and Nanniah, 

From there, we drove to Auckland airport, enjoying the orange sunset hues of the sky. We bid by to Nanniah, dropped of cab and boarded the flight with heavy memories.
It was also harder than any other trip of ours because this was this years last trip with Rinku and Farini as they were moving to US in a month or two. 

So Until next time, Mā te wā (see ya next time)

What a bittersweet way to end — Uno cards in the park, pizza, gelato, and knowing it's the last trip with Rinku and Farini before they move. "Mā te wā" is such a lovely closer.

Okay, we've covered the whole journey! Let's wrap this up properly. A few final questions:

1. If you had to pick ONE single best moment of the entire 14 days, what would it be?
2. What's one thing you'd tell a friend NOT to do (a mistake or regret)?
3. Quick must-visit vs overrated/skip list — any places you'd tell someone to definitely see, and any that weren't worth it?

best moment? of course, driving ̉RV in an unknown land and Nevis jump, scary, yet something I am proud of doing it

Def not to opt out for a campervan cleaning package, lol

wanaka tree is overrated, indeed we skipped it, must visit is treks in Mt Cook, plz do if someone loves treks and ferg burger and monk cod in queenstown

Perfect, that's gold for the Tips and Must Visit sections!

Last thing — give me the quick city-to-city itinerary route for the blog (like Christchurch → Lake Tekapo → Twizel → ... → Auckland), just the path you took.

you build the city to city itinerry based on info you have and ensure you add website for britz, and all apps we used campermate and for fuel Gaspy which is very much used to figure out cheap fuel places and for esim, we used mobimatter
Got everything I need! Writing your blog now...

excerpt: "Mattuuuu, are you excited to visit your favorite country?" 14 days, one campervan and four clueless Indians across New Zealand: bungee, skydives, glaciers, dolphins and a blood moon.

items: Do NOT skip the campervan cleaning package. It's my single biggest regret. Britz charges around 250 NZD (~₹13,000) to take the van back as-is: no cleaning, no gas or fuel refills.
Reach the rental office on time.

Install these before you land: CamperMate (campermate.com) for campsites, dump stations, water refills and toilets; 
Gaspy (gaspy.nz) for the cheapest fuel near you, since prices swing a lot between stations; and MobiMatter (mobimatter.com) for the eSIM.
Free campsites (DOC sites and freedom camping spots) really are free, with lakeside views no paid site can match.
Community pools are the shower hack: 3–5 NZD (~₹150–250) per person for a swim and a hot shower.

Get the direction right. Don't do campervan in the South; fly to Auckland and rent a car for the North like we did; we lost a full day. Pick up in Auckland, drive south, take the ferry across, and finish in Christchurch, especially if Wharariki and Kaikōura are on your list.
If you do one bungee in your life, make it Nevis: 143 m against Kawarau's 43 m. Scared of heights like me? Pay first, panic later. You won't back out once the money is gone.
Hell's Gate mud spa: maybe skip. Three of us itched for hours and Rinku fell sick.
Overrated: the Wanaka Tree. It's a tree in water. We skipped it with zero regrets.
